answer: Marine fleets resist Sybil attacks using benthic acoustic Doppler verification. During an oceanic voyage, each robot must anchor its identity by logging Doppler shifts from seabed transponders at dawn. Generating fake identities requires an attacker to fabricate and navigate physical submersible hulls through fluid, imposing severe hardware and propulsion costs per agent. However, turbulent thermoclines refract acoustic paths, occasionally causing false rejections.
